title: 2026 HSE permit surrender and revocation QA

facts.source_fact: Where an installation has ceased operation, the operator must apply through METS to surrender the permit by the relevant surrender date or a later date agreed with the regulator.
If the regulator has issued a notice determining cessation, the relevant surrender date is one month from that notice.
Otherwise the surrender date is based on the later of one month from cessation or one month from the date the operator no longer intends regulated activities to resume.
A surrender application is not itself a restart authorisation.
If activity is to restart after surrender, a permit must be re-applied for and be in force before regulated activity restarts.
After surrendering an HSE permit, re-entry during 2026–2030 requires a GHGE permit because there is no provision to re-enter as HSE in that period.
The regulator may revoke a permit for failure to comply with UK ETS obligations or failure to pay the subsistence fee.
The regulator must revoke the permit if surrender is required and the operator does not apply on time.
Surrender or revocation results in a surrender notice or revocation notice.
The notice includes requirements such as reporting reportable emissions up to the date the notice takes effect.
